text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a software development practice where developers regularly merge their code changes into a shared main repository. Instead of waiting to combine all work at the end, every small change triggers an automated build. This means the code is compiled automatically, and then a suite of tests runs on it immediately. The main benefit of this process is catching issues early. If a new code change accidentally breaks an existing feature or causes an error, the team finds out within minutes. These automated steps are managed by a CI pipeline, which acts like a checklist that ensures every update meets basic quality standards before moving forward.
